Some robotics problems look simple — until you try to control them.

The Double Pendulum is one of those problems.
Two links.
Two joints.
Coupled dynamics.
Nonlinear behavior.

And suddenly, a system that looks simple becomes a serious control and simulation challenge.
What I find interesting about projects like this is the connection between mathematical modeling and real-world robotics.

You can approach the same system through:
🔹 Mathematical / code-based modeling
🔹 MATLAB simulation
🔹 Simulink block-based modeling
🔹 Simscape physical modeling

Each approach gives a different perspective on how the system behaves.
The real learning happens when you move beyond simply getting a 

simulation to run and start asking:
Why is the system behaving this way?
How do the dynamics change?
How can we control it?

What happens when real-world constraints are introduced?
This is exactly the kind of engineering thinking we want to encourage through KLS – KEP Labs Simulator.

At KEP, we are working toward a virtual engineering environment where students and engineers can model, simulate, experiment, debug, and validate complex systems before moving to physical hardware.

From simple circuits to robotic mechanisms, from sensors to control systems — simulation should become a part of the engineering workflow, not just a classroom exercise.

Learn the theory.
Build the model.
Run the simulation.
Understand the behavior.
Then build it in the real world.
That is the mindset we are building with KLS. 🚀

Some robotics problems look simple — until you try to control them.

The Double Pendulum is one of those problems.
Two links.
Two joints.
Coupled dynamics.
Nonlinear behavior.

And suddenly, a system that looks simple becomes a serious control and simulation challenge.
What I find interesting about projects like this is the connection between mathematical modeling and real-world robotics.

You can approach the same system through:
🔹 Mathematical / code-based modeling
🔹 MATLAB simulation
🔹 Simulink block-based modeling
🔹 Simscape physical modeling

Each approach gives a different perspective on how the system behaves.
The real learning happens when you move beyond simply getting a 

simulation to run and start asking:
Why is the system behaving this way?
How do the dynamics change?
How can we control it?

What happens when real-world constraints are introduced?
This is exactly the kind of engineering thinking we want to encourage through KLS – KEP Labs Simulator.

At KEP, we are working toward a virtual engineering environment where students and engineers can model, simulate, experiment, debug, and validate complex systems before moving to physical hardware.

From simple circuits to robotic mechanisms, from sensors to control systems — simulation should become a part of the engineering workflow, not just a classroom exercise.

Learn the theory.
Build the model.
Run the simulation.
Understand the behavior.
Then build it in the real world.
That is the mindset we are building with KLS. 🚀

Some robotics problems look simple — until you try to control them.

The Double Pendulum is one of those problems.
Two links.
Two joints.
Coupled dynamics.
Nonlinear behavior.

And suddenly, a system that looks simple becomes a serious control and simulation challenge.
What I find interesting about projects like this is the connection between mathematical modeling and real-world robotics.

You can approach the same system through:
🔹 Mathematical / code-based modeling
🔹 MATLAB simulation
🔹 Simulink block-based modeling
🔹 Simscape physical modeling

Each approach gives a different perspective on how the system behaves.
The real learning happens when you move beyond simply getting a 

simulation to run and start asking:
Why is the system behaving this way?
How do the dynamics change?
How can we control it?

What happens when real-world constraints are introduced?
This is exactly the kind of engineering thinking we want to encourage through KLS – KEP Labs Simulator.

At KEP, we are working toward a virtual engineering environment where students and engineers can model, simulate, experiment, debug, and validate complex systems before moving to physical hardware.

From simple circuits to robotic mechanisms, from sensors to control systems — simulation should become a part of the engineering workflow, not just a classroom exercise.

Learn the theory.
Build the model.
Run the simulation.
Understand the behavior.
Then build it in the real world.
That is the mindset we are building with KLS. 🚀

Congratulations to Syed Ali, Reza Kazerounian, and the entire Alif Semiconductor team on their acquisition by Analog Devices for over $1.6 billion.

Alif built for that future from day one. Its AI-native microcontrollers (MCUs) and fusion processors are for edge devices such as wearables, hearables, smart glasses, cameras, medical devices, industrial sensors, security systems, and smart home products.

Unlike a conventional MCU, Alif integrates CPUs, dedicated neural-processing units, memory, security, connectivity, and aggressive power management into a single chip.

As models get smaller and NPUs more efficient, privacy, latency, and cloud economics are pushing more inference to the edge. Alif saw that shift early and built the silicon to power it.

We also believed deeply in the team. Syed previously co-founded and led Cavium through its $6 billion acquisition by Marvell. Reza built and ran multibillion-dollar semiconductor businesses at Freescale and STMicroelectronics. Together, they brought the vision, experience, and conviction required to build foundational technology ahead of the market.

Some robotics problems look simple — until you try to control them.

The Double Pendulum is one of those problems.
Two links.
Two joints.
Coupled dynamics.
Nonlinear behavior.

And suddenly, a system that looks simple becomes a serious control and simulation challenge.
What I find interesting about projects like this is the connection between mathematical modeling and real-world robotics.

You can approach the same system through:
🔹 Mathematical / code-based modeling
🔹 MATLAB simulation
🔹 Simulink block-based modeling
🔹 Simscape physical modeling

Each approach gives a different perspective on how the system behaves.
The real learning happens when you move beyond simply getting a 

simulation to run and start asking:
Why is the system behaving this way?
How do the dynamics change?
How can we control it?

What happens when real-world constraints are introduced?
This is exactly the kind of engineering thinking we want to encourage through KLS – KEP Labs Simulator.

At KEP, we are working toward a virtual engineering environment where students and engineers can model, simulate, experiment, debug, and validate complex systems before moving to physical hardware.

From simple circuits to robotic mechanisms, from sensors to control systems — simulation should become a part of the engineering workflow, not just a classroom exercise.

Learn the theory.
Build the model.
Run the simulation.
Understand the behavior.
Then build it in the real world.
That is the mindset we are building with KLS. 🚀

The Dawn of Next-Gen Intelligence: Exploring OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra

Artificial intelligence continues to evolve at an unprecedented pace, and the unveiling of GPT-6 Astra marks another monumental milestone in the journey toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). As the latest flagship foundation model from OpenAI, GPT-6 Astra introduces fundamental architectural breakthroughs in native multi-modal reasoning, autonomous agentic workflows, extreme compute efficiency, and continuous real-time context synthesis.

1. True Native Omnimodality
Unlike legacy architectures that relied on separate tokenizers or modality bridging adapters, GPT-6 Astra is trained natively from the ground up on continuous high-frequency video, spatial audio, symbolic code, and telemetry sensor streams. This architectural shift enables Astra to perceive, interpret, and reason across real-world physical and digital environments with sub-millisecond latency. Whether analyzing complex surgical video feeds, debugging distributed cloud infrastructure, or modeling macroeconomic market movements, Astra processes cross-modal contexts natively with zero fidelity degradation.

2. Dynamic Recursive Reasoning & Verifiable Self-Correction
One of the persistent limitations of earlier transformer generations was linear, autoregressive generation without real-time reflection. GPT-6 Astra solves this challenge through an embedded dynamic recursive reasoning core. Astra actively simulates multiple downstream solution trees, verifies intermediate logical assertions against formal execution engines, and autonomously backtracks when anomalies are detected. This mechanism drastically curtails hallucination rates, establishing unprecedented accuracy benchmarks across advanced theoretical mathematics, mission-critical systems engineering, and formal logic synthesis.

3. Autonomous Agentic Coordination and Tool Synthesis
GPT-6 Astra is designed not merely as a conversational assistant, but as an enterprise-grade autonomous coordination engine. Featuring built-in multi-agent swarm orchestration, Astra can seamlessly decompose high-level business objectives into thousands of parallel, self-directed sub-tasks. The model creates custom APIs and executable tools on the fly, persists dynamic task memory across weeks of execution, and self-heals broken pipelines. From full-stack enterprise software maintenance to automated biochemical research workflows, Astra bridges the gap between abstract strategy and operational completion.

4. 10 Million+ Ultra-Long Context Window
Context boundaries have been redefined. Leveraging novel sparse attention algorithms and hierarchical memory retrieval structures, Astra supports active working contexts surpassing 10 million tokens. Entire enterprise repositories, complete legal case law archives, and decades of financial filings can now be queried and cross-analyzed instantly with perfect retrieval fidelity.

5. Enterprise Safety, Governance, and Real-Time Adaptation
Safety and alignment are integrated directly into the core inference layer. Astra features runtime constitutional guardrails, ensuring provable compliance, data privacy, and zero data leakage. Organizations can define deterministic policy constraints while Astra adapts to localized domain vernacular in real time.

Conclusion
GPT-6 Astra represents a profound leap forward in computational intelligence. By harmonizing native multimodality, rigorous self-correction, and autonomous execution, it redefines what is possible across technology, science, and human ingenuity.

The Next Frontier of Artificial General Intelligence: Exploring GPT-6 Astra

Artificial Intelligence has advanced at a breakneck pace over the past few years, evolving from rudimentary text generators into sophisticated multi-modal cognitive architectures. Just as the global technology community adapted to the paradigm shifts introduced by previous generations, OpenAI has officially unveiled its most transformative foundation model to date: GPT-6 Astra.

GPT-6 Astra represents a monumental leap forward, not merely in terms of raw compute and parameter scale, but fundamentally in architectural design, autonomous reasoning, and native multi-sensory understanding. It marks a decisive transition from reactive chatbots to proactive, high-order reasoning partners capable of operating across complex, open-ended environments.

1. Native Multi-Modal Grounding and Fluid Interaction
Unlike prior models that stitched separate modalities together through post-training adapters, GPT-6 Astra was trained natively from the ground up across unified omni-modal data streams: continuous high-resolution video feeds, spatial audio, multi-lingual text, system-level code, symbolic mathematics, and real-time physical sensor telemetry. This gives Astra an unprecedented contextual awareness of the physical world, effectively bridging the gap between digital cognitive processing and embodied physical intelligence.

2. Dynamic Autonomous Reasoning and Self-Reflective Loops
Astra introduces a breakthrough internal mechanism known as the Self-Correction and Dynamic Latent Planning loop. Rather than generating responses token by token based strictly on immediate statistical probability, Astra actively simulates multiple downstream execution paths in high-dimensional latent space. It tests hypotheses, audits sandboxed code executions internally, verifies logic constraints, and autonomously corrects its own reasoning before presenting a final output. This slashes hallucination rates to near-zero in mission-critical domains such as automated software engineering, precision healthcare diagnostics, and complex legal analysis.

3. Hyper-Efficiency via Sparse Dynamic Routing
Scaling massive architectures traditionally poses severe computational and energy challenges. GPT-6 Astra integrates revolutionary dynamic routing algorithms that activate only a specific, highly optimized fraction of its multi-trillion parameter core per query. This sparse execution model delivers up to a tenfold increase in throughput while drastically reducing inference latency and carbon footprint, making enterprise-grade real-time autonomous agents economically viable for production deployment worldwide.

4. Revolutionizing Enterprise Automation and Systemic Workflows
The implications for industry are profound. With Astra, software development shifts from human-written code assisted by copilots to full-scale autonomous engineering teams capable of architecting, testing, deploying, and maintaining entire distributed cloud infrastructures. In life sciences, Astra accelerates molecular dynamics modeling and therapeutic drug discovery pipelines from years to hours. In business operations, it unifies fragmented organizational data and executes complex cross-platform workflows with exceptional precision.

5. Ethical Alignment, Safety, and Verifiable Guardrails
With enormous capability comes the imperative for rigorous governance. OpenAI has integrated mathematical verification techniques into Astra’s safety layers, establishing deterministic guarantees against prompt injection, data exfiltration, and unintended policy violations.

Conclusion
GPT-6 Astra is not just another incremental update; it represents the dawn of genuinely proactive, autonomous AI systems designed to augment human potential and accelerate human progress across every scientific and technological endeavor.

🚀 Thrilled to announce the successful completion of our working prototype for Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2026 Problem Statement 26171!

What started as an ambitious idea has now evolved far beyond just a proof of concept. I am proud to share that our team has developed not only a fully functional working prototype and a Minimum Viable Product (MVP), but also a comprehensive, highly resilient, and production-grade application ready for large-scale deployment.

Key highlights of our architecture and solution:

1. End-to-End System Integration: Built on a modern, cloud-native microservices architecture ensuring high availability, fault tolerance, and near-zero latency processing.
2. Robust MVP & Production Readiness: We transitioned rapidly from early validation to implementing rigorous enterprise-grade security protocols, automated CI/CD pipelines, containerization using Docker and Kubernetes, and real-time observability.
3. Scalable Core Functionality: The system seamlessly addresses all critical requirements outlined in Problem Statement 26171, handling high-concurrency workloads, data integrity verification, and dynamic analytics dashboards with peak efficiency.
4. User-Centric Design: Clean, accessible, and intuitive UI/UX engineered for both end-users and administrators, providing frictionless onboarding, deep actionable insights, and robust governance tools.

This journey pushed our technical boundaries across full-stack engineering, distributed systems, and real-world system design. Going from requirement analysis to a battle-tested production release demonstrates the immense power of disciplined execution, rapid prototyping, and scalable software architecture.

A huge thank you to our mentors, teammates, and peers for the relentless support throughout this milestone! Looking forward to driving impactful technological transformation and scaling this solution further.

Key Highlights of Our Solution for Problem Statement 26171:
1. End-to-End Architecture: Built with a modern microservices pattern, decoupled frontend and backend services, robust API gateways, and enterprise-grade data management pipelines.
2. Production-Grade Engineering: Designed for high availability, fault tolerance, low-latency data processing, and seamless horizontal scalability under heavy user load.
3. Security & Compliance: Integrated comprehensive authentication, role-based access control (RBAC), end-to-end data encryption, and full compliance with industry security best practices.
4. User Experience: Developed an intuitive, accessible, and responsive user interface tailored to streamline workflow efficiency and maximize user engagement across web and mobile platforms.
5. Automated CI/CD & Monitoring: Deployed automated testing suites, continuous integration pipelines, real-time logging, metrics collection, and alerting systems to ensure uninterrupted system health.

This milestone demonstrates that we are not just solving theoretical challenges, but delivering complete, resilient, and enterprise-ready software solutions capable of driving tangible national impact.

A huge thank you to my team, mentors, and the entire SIH community for their continuous support and guidance throughout this journey!

Smart India Hackathon (SIH 2026): Navigating Screening vs. Final Evaluation

As excitement builds around SIH 2026, understanding the distinct criteria between initial screening and final evaluation stages is key for participating teams.

1. Preliminary Screening: Conceptual Clarity & Viability
The screening phase focuses on problem understanding, innovation, and theoretical feasibility. Evaluators review submitted PPTs to filter out thousands of entries. Key metrics include:
- Novelty of the approach.
- Direct alignment with the ministry/industry problem statement.
- Technical architecture and realistic roadmap.
Clarity and structure win over complex jargon.

2. Final Evaluation: Working Prototype & Real-World Impact
During the Grand Finale, the dynamics shift drastically. Evaluators and ministry officials scrutinize execution:
- Functional prototype robustness (UI/UX, backend scalability, edge cases).
- Commercial viability, cost analysis, and scalability.
- Live demonstration under pressure and rapid implementation of mentor feedback.

While screening tests vision and planning, final evaluation tests engineering grit and delivery. Bridge the gap between pitch decks and production-ready code!

Today, our campus is buzzing with immense energy, passion, and intense brainstorming sessions as dozens of brilliant teams come together to tackle pressing real-world challenges across various problem statements given by ministries, departments, and industry leaders.

From early morning, student developers, designers, and innovators have been collaborating, architecting software architectures, coding web applications, training artificial intelligence models, configuring IoT devices, and designing clean user interfaces. The atmosphere is filled with pure enthusiasm and the spirit of innovation. Teams are working relentlessly to convert ambitious concepts into viable, impactful working prototypes.

Hackathons like SIH offer a tremendous platform to test our technical limits, foster teamwork, refine our presentation skills, and build scalable solutions that can make a genuine difference in society. It is truly inspiring to witness the level of creativity, dedication, and problem-solving mindset demonstrated by each participant today.

A huge thank you to our esteemed faculty coordinators, mentors, and student organizers whose tireless support has made this internal round smooth, dynamic, and productive. Wishing all the participating teams the absolute best of luck as they pitch their groundbreaking ideas to the evaluation jury. May the most innovative solutions advance to represent our institution at the national level!

Disclaimer

This project was created for a computer science class at PCSI Déodat de Séverac in Toulouse. While the code structure and versioning may be unconventional, it serves as a proof of concept for what could have been an exciting sandbox space game. We thank you for your support and feedback which helped us a lot during development, this project is now officially dead and burried. However, if you're interested in the game genre, this project was heavily inspired by Universe Sandbox1, a game by Giant Army, which you should definitely check out 🚀

V 0.10-alpha



A brand new menu has been added, with 3d animations and stuff, we hope you like it (see project for more to-do-list info). Our current goal is to create realistic impact particles, using the integrated panda3d particle generator, which will contribute to the realism of the game and allow us to consider working on a well thought HUD for the players. It is possible to import 3d models and test simulations using those, but it is very hard to master though, as I haven't created a syntax guide for users. If you still wish to do so, please contact us by creating a new issue

Some screenshots

 

Installing test versions

It is not recommended to use versions other than the ones merged into the master branch. Most of the other branches contain outdated or unstable versions, that may not be safe for common usage. However, if you wish to test our last commits, or simply read the code, please feel free to press the [Clone or download] button. Executing the code requires a basic python IDE, and the panda3d library. Install it through the windows cmd or whatever shell you use: pip install panda3d==1.10.3

it is also necessary that you have the pypresence lib working on your machine, repeat the same process to install it: pip install pypresence

Installation

Just download the latest release, extract the files, and run the PyOS.exe file (if you're using windows, if you have linux or mac, just go to the correct folder). There are no other requirements for this program to work

Contribution to the building of the project

If you find what seems to be a bug, and is not listed in the To-do-list, please be kind and report it in the issues section, we will definitely appreciate your help.

Disclaimer

This project was created for a computer science class at PCSI Déodat de Séverac in Toulouse. While the code structure and versioning may be unconventional, it serves as a proof of concept for what could have been an exciting sandbox space game. We thank you for your support and feedback which helped us a lot during development, this project is now officially dead and burried. However, if you're interested in the game genre, this project was heavily inspired by Universe Sandbox1, a game by Giant Army, which you should definitely check out 🚀

V 0.10-alpha



A brand new menu has been added, with 3d animations and stuff, we hope you like it (see project for more to-do-list info). Our current goal is to create realistic impact particles, using the integrated panda3d particle generator, which will contribute to the realism of the game and allow us to consider working on a well thought HUD for the players. It is possible to import 3d models and test simulations using those, but it is very hard to master though, as I haven't created a syntax guide for users. If you still wish to do so, please contact us by creating a new issue

Some screenshots

 

Installing test versions

It is not recommended to use versions other than the ones merged into the master branch. Most of the other branches contain outdated or unstable versions, that may not be safe for common usage. However, if you wish to test our last commits, or simply read the code, please feel free to press the [Clone or download] button. Executing the code requires a basic python IDE, and the panda3d library. Install it through the windows cmd or whatever shell you use: pip install panda3d==1.10.3

it is also necessary that you have the pypresence lib working on your machine, repeat the same process to install it: pip install pypresence

Installation

Just download the latest release, extract the files, and run the PyOS.exe file (if you're using windows, if you have linux or mac, just go to the correct folder). There are no other requirements for this program to work

Contribution to the building of the project

If you find what seems to be a bug, and is not listed in the To-do-list, please be kind and report it in the issues section, we will definitely appreciate your help.

Chandrayaan-2

The Chandrayaan-2 mission was successfully launched on 22nd July 2019 at 14:43 hrs by GSLV MkIII-M1 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota. After a series of Earth bound manoeuvres, the spacecraft entered into Lunar Transfer Trajectory (LTT) on August 14th. Lunar Orbit Insertion (LOI) manoeuvre was performed on August 20th, thereby Chandrayaan-2 was successfully inserted into the elliptical orbit around the Moon. This was followed by a series of Lunar bound orbit maneuvers for reducing the orbit to circular polar orbit around the Moon. Know more

Mission Objectives:

To develop and demonstrate the key technologies for end-to-end lunar mission capability, including soft-landing and roving on the lunar surface.

Science Objectives:

To expand the lunar scientific knowledge through detailed study of topography, mineralogy, surface chemical composition, thermo-physical characteristics and tenuous lunar atmosphere leading to a better understanding of the origin and evolution of the Moon.

Payloads

Chandrayaan-2's science payloads aim to perform detailed study of lunar topography, seismography, mineral identification & distribution, surface chemical composition, thermo-physical characteristics of top soil & composition of the tenuous lunar atmosphere. Know More

Brochure

Chandrayaan-2 brochure comprising of information on why are we going to moon, it's flight sequence, GSLV-Mk-III, mission sequence, CH2 composite module, orbiter, lander, rover and mission payloads is Available here

Data

The data acquired at various phases of the Chandrayaan-2 mission from CLASS, CHACE-2, XSM , IIRS, TMC-2, OHRC, DFRS and DFSAR are processed as per the processing level definitions and provided in Planetary Data System (PDS) standards for archival and dissemination. Access here

About PRADAN
PRADAN is a web application developed by ISSDC to serve the data archived at ISSDC to its user, with basic features being the ease to search and browse through the data before downloading. It provides single sign-on (SSO) feature for all data sets hosted on PRADAN, i.e. once the user logs-in to access any of the data sets, all other data sets hosted on PRADAN also become accessible without requiring user to re-enter the login credentials. PRADAN stands for Policy based data Retrieval, Analytics, Dissemination And Notification system.
